note.note:
History:
- Main complaint: Swelling of left elbow noticed about 1 week ago.
- Onset & duration: Swelling appeared approximately 7 days prior to consult; first occurrence.
- Symptoms: Swelling is slightly warm, feels as though there is fluid inside; not painful; no significant tenderness except a “weird” sensation when pressing near the swelling; normal range of motion.
- Associated symptoms: No systemic symptoms reported. No pain, trauma, redness, or prior episodes.
- Context: Noticed swelling during shower; patient has a sedentary office job; no history of trauma or repetitive physical activity.
- Family history: Unclear; patient uncertain but no known family rheumatological conditions.
- Relevant negatives: No history of eczema or other skin disorders.

Past Medical History:
- Osteoarthritis, diagnosed by a GP a few years ago.
- Allergy to peanuts.
- No medication allergies.
- No regular medications.
- Generally fit and well; runs 2-3 times per week.
- No other illnesses or relevant medical history.

Physical Examination:
- Visual inspection via video: Swelling observed over left elbow, skin over tip appears dry.
- Swelling slightly warm compared to adjacent skin.
- No major tenderness at the tip, slight discomfort near area of swelling.
- Full, normal range of motion at elbow.
- No mention of erythema or spreading redness.
- No evidence or report of systemic illness.
- No skin dryness elsewhere, no eczema.
- Alert and oriented.

Impression:
- Suspected left olecranon bursitis (inflammation of the bursa over the elbow).

Management Plan:
- Advised to begin ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily after food; over-the-counter (dose/route/frequency documented).
- Stop ibuprofen if heartburn occurs.
- Blood tests ordered: Inflammatory markers, infection screening, rheumatological antibodies, evaluation for gout.
- Blood test forms to be mailed to patient with instructions for completion.
- Follow-up appointment arranged after test results—can be telephone, video, or face-to-face as preferred.
- Emergency advice: Return urgently if elbow becomes very red, very painful, or swelling spreads—concern for septic arthritis in that scenario.

Patient Summary:
- 53-year-old male presented with a week-long, painless, mildly warm swelling over the left elbow, with preserved function and no systemic symptoms. Clinical findings consistent with non-infective bursitis; treated conservatively with NSAIDs and further investigations for possible underlying causes. Urgent review advised if signs of infection develop.

Key Takeaways:
- Take ibuprofen 400 mg twice a day after food; discontinue if heartburn occurs.
- Complete blood tests as soon as forms are received.
- Seek urgent medical attention if elbow becomes more red, painful, or if redness spreads.

Next Steps:
- Patient to complete blood tests when forms arrive.
- Arrange follow-up consultation (phone, video, or in-person) after results are available.
- Monitor for signs of infection or worsening symptoms requiring urgent review.
